name: CodePilot
description: Local engineering workflow CLI that turns natural-language requirements into tasks and coordinates planning, execution, review, operations, and release.
calling_principles: Prefer non-interactive commands and avoid chat mode unless a persistent conversation is explicitly needed.
When structured output is needed, prefer `hud --json`, `status --json`, `task show --json`, `doctor --json`, `task find --json`, or `ai manifest`.
To submit a natural-language requirement, call `codepilot "requirement text"` or `codepilot go "requirement text"`.
Chat, Web UI sessions, and Feishu free text route through the OpenCode agent; CodePilot provides MCP workflow tools and project constraints.
Call `plan`, `inspect --write-workflow`, or MCP workflow tools explicitly when deterministic artifacts are required.

Advance `plan` / `inspect` `next_actions` with `workflow next --list` / `workflow next --action <id>`; `workflow next --auto` only chooses policy-allowed actions and defaults do not create or import tasks; treat `suggested_command` as display/review metadata only.
For project state, task counts, completion ratio, failed tasks, running tasks, or service status, let the agent choose `status`, `hud`, `task`, or `trace` tools.
For release artifacts, prefer `codepilot binary prepare --version <version>`.
If a task is running, inspect its phase with `codepilot status -p <project-name> -v` before deciding whether to view logs or stop it.
If a failed task needs a full repair loop, prefer `codepilot build-fix -p <project-name> --task-id <task_id> --json`; use `codepilot task retry <task_id>` only to requeue it.

commands.name: init
commands.purpose: Initialize a project and generate AGENTS.toml.
commands.when_to_use: Use when connecting a repository for the first time.

commands.name: setup
commands.purpose: Prepare project .codepilot state, sync AGENTS.toml, and register the project.
commands.when_to_use: Use before installing hooks or when preparing CodePilot project state.

commands.name: self_update
commands.purpose: Run a project-local self-improvement dry run that collects evidence and produces an upgrade plan without changing code.
commands.when_to_use: Use when CodePilot should audit its own project state before creating tasks or making changes.

commands.name: goal
commands.purpose: Submit a natural-language requirement for planning and optional execution.
commands.when_to_use: Use when another AI wants CodePilot to own the implementation workflow.
examples: codepilot "Fix task retry logic and add tests"

commands.name: go
commands.purpose: Explicit requirement entrypoint for planning and execution.
commands.when_to_use: Use when project/planner/executor options must be explicit.
examples: codepilot go "Fix task retry logic and add tests" -p <project-name>

commands.name: chat
commands.purpose: Start the CodePilot-managed OpenCode TUI with isolated config, MCP, commands, provider/model, and permissions.
commands.when_to_use: Use for persistent interactive sessions.

commands.name: status
commands.purpose: Show task overview, running state, and latest output.
commands.when_to_use: Use to check backlog, stuck tasks, or active phases.

commands.name: hud
commands.purpose: Show a lightweight workflow HUD with queue, running tasks, activity, and services.
commands.when_to_use: Use for quick workspace health checks.

commands.name: task_logs
commands.purpose: Read real-time or historical task logs.
commands.when_to_use: Use for task execution details and error context.

commands.name: task_show
commands.purpose: Read full task metadata, content, errors, delivery record, and log summary.
commands.when_to_use: Use when the exact task id is known.

commands.name: task_retry
commands.purpose: Reset a failed/cancelled task and put it back into backlog.
commands.when_to_use: Use for manual requeueing.

commands.name: task_stop
commands.purpose: Stop a running task.
commands.when_to_use: Use when a task is stuck or going in the wrong direction.

commands.name: run
commands.purpose: Execute backlog tasks.
commands.when_to_use: Use when tasks already exist and should run now.

commands.name: build_fix
commands.purpose: Collect failure context, retry repair, run validation, and produce a verdict.
commands.when_to_use: Use when failed tasks need a complete repair loop.

commands.name: doctor
commands.purpose: Check environment, configuration, CLI tools, API keys, database, and services.
commands.when_to_use: Use for environment or setup troubleshooting.

commands.name: inspect
commands.purpose: Inspect project signals, preview candidates, optionally write workflow context, or create candidate tasks.
commands.when_to_use: Use to discover technical debt, failed-task patterns, and improvement candidates; the default --dry-run path does not create backlog tasks.

commands.name: explore
commands.purpose: Read-only exploration of files, Git, task logs, wiki, and inspect signals.
commands.when_to_use: Use when planning needs local evidence but should not modify anything.

commands.name: plan
commands.purpose: Generate a reviewable plan artifact with scope, risks, verification matrix, and task candidates.
commands.when_to_use: Use when requirements are ready for plan review but should not enter backlog.

commands.name: workflow_auto_policy
commands.purpose: Return the resolved auto-advance policy: allow_create_inspect_tasks, allow_import_plan_tasks, max_steps, failure_threshold.
commands.when_to_use: Use before --auto to check whether inspect task creation or plan task import is allowed by project configuration.

commands.name: workflow_status
commands.purpose: Read latest or mode-specific workflow state and agent session context, including artifact paths, next-action source, and auto_policy.
commands.when_to_use: Use before advancing a plan/inspect artifact or when inspecting current workflow state.

commands.name: workflow_next
commands.purpose: List, safely execute, or policy-auto-advance artifact next_actions through a fixed allowlist; it never executes suggested_command strings.
commands.when_to_use: Use after plan/inspect returns next_actions and an external agent needs to advance by action id or let CodePilot choose policy-allowed auto actions. Defaults do not create inspect tasks or import plan tasks unless AGENTS.toml opts in.

commands.name: wiki
commands.purpose: Maintain local Markdown project knowledge.
commands.when_to_use: Use to record or query build commands, architecture facts, failure modes, and decisions.

commands.name: note
commands.purpose: Maintain persistent project working memory.
commands.when_to_use: Use to preserve important context across sessions.
examples: codepilot note add -p <project-name> "pytest -q is the main validation command"

commands.name: memory
commands.purpose: Read project-local factual memory events; CodePilot automatically creates deduplicated candidates with score/feedback/seen_count and `.codepilot/memory/autocapture.md`.
commands.when_to_use: Use to analyze inspect/workflow events and self-improvement evidence.

commands.name: trace
commands.purpose: Show recent activity across task lifecycle, logs, service heartbeats, and workflow state.
commands.when_to_use: Use to understand what happened recently.

commands.name: ui
commands.purpose: Run or manage the Web UI.
commands.when_to_use: Use for graphical multi-project overview or persistent UI service management.

commands.name: shutdown
commands.purpose: Stop CodePilot Web UI, Feishu, webhook, daemon, inspect, and active task runtime processes in one operation.
commands.when_to_use: Use when local CodePilot services should be shut down and active work should either finish gracefully or be force-stopped.

commands.name: daemon
commands.purpose: Continuously poll backlog and execute tasks for a project.
commands.when_to_use: Use when tasks should run continuously in the background.

commands.name: event
commands.purpose: Manage project event sink registry and event schema.
commands.when_to_use: Use for hook/event plugin integration.

commands.name: hook
commands.purpose: Manage project hook registry and lifecycle event validation.
commands.when_to_use: Use to verify hook/event integrations.

commands.name: exec
commands.purpose: Run provider-neutral command smoke checks with project-local audit events.
commands.when_to_use: Use to verify agent CLIs or custom commands in project context.

commands.name: skill
commands.purpose: Manage and run local workflow skill catalog entries.
commands.when_to_use: Use to discover or run project workflow skills.

commands.name: webhook
commands.purpose: Start the lightweight HTTP webhook service.
commands.when_to_use: Use when external systems need to POST tasks or receive status notifications.

commands.name: feishu
commands.purpose: Manage the Feishu long-connection bot.
commands.when_to_use: Use for Feishu status cards, Q&A, task control, and notifications.

commands.name: binary_prepare
commands.purpose: Update version, build the current platform, generate a release directory, and verify it.
commands.when_to_use: Use to prepare a local release package.

commands.name: binary_release
commands.purpose: Assemble existing binaries into a standard release directory.
commands.when_to_use: Use when preparing artifacts for release.

commands.name: binary_verify
commands.purpose: Verify release directory, archives, and checksums.
commands.when_to_use: Use before publishing.

commands.name: ai_template
commands.purpose: Return the task template, machine-readable schema, or filling guide.
commands.when_to_use: Use before external AI batch-imports tasks with `add -f`.

workflows.name: Submit and execute a new requirement
Use the OpenCode workflow in chat or Feishu
steps: Ask about project state directly; the OpenCode agent chooses CodePilot MCP tools.
Submit requirements as natural language; OpenCode can call CodePilot MCP planning and task tools.
Use explicit operations like `retry 123` or `tasks failed`, or describe the operation in natural language.
Call `plan` explicitly when deterministic artifacts are needed.

steps: # Choose an action id from the list; do not execute suggested_command strings.
